task: Turn spawned qrexec crash-boundary evidence into a bounded, SHA-bound transport qualification artifact without overstating exactly-once semantics.

attempts: Treat test pass/fail alone as the qualification authority.
Summarize only successful crash cases and infer transport readiness.
Require a fixed complete scenario set with explicit postconditions and duplicate-mutation counters.
correctness.reason: Readiness becomes a deterministic function of all required crash boundaries. Before-mutation, post-claim, post-heartbeat, post-fail, post-complete, and post-journal-commit outcomes cannot be omitted or silently reclassified.

attempts: Store raw request/response payloads in the qualification report.
Store only boolean outcome/attestation facts and crash-safety counters in a canonical digest-bound report.
Sign the local report with a new private key.
robustnessSecurity.reason: The report avoids lease tokens, request MACs, private-key material, mission payloads, and stack traces. SHA-256 provides tamper/comparison integrity without introducing another key lifecycle. Ed25519 authenticity remains verified at each protocol response before the report records attestationVerified=true.

attempts: Add a new transport telemetry daemon or persistent database.
Re-run extra qrexec probes solely to populate the report.
Build the report from existing spawned crash-campaign outputs offline.
latencyResourcesRegression.winner: offline qualification report over existing evidence
latencyResourcesRegression.reason: Adds zero production qrexec round trips, zero coordinator mutations, no daemon/database, and negligible local CPU/memory. It preserves current crash semantics instead of widening MissionQueue or WorkerRuntime behavior.

winner: Schema-v1 offline transport qualification artifact bound to exact Git SHA, runtime fingerprint, complete crash scenario set, zero duplicate-mutation counters, response-attestation verification, and canonical SHA-256 evidence digest.
qa: All six required crash scenarios must be present; missing or extra scenarios fail closed.
beforeMutation requires zero durable effects and a clean retry-once outcome.
claim/heartbeat/fail post-mutation deaths require exactly one durable effect, pending journal, attested REQUEST_OUTCOME_INDETERMINATE, and zero duplicate mutation.
complete post-mutation death requires exactly one durable effect and read-only reconciled committed completion.
post-journal-commit death requires replay of the committed result without a second mutation.
Every protocol response used by qualification must already have a verified request-bound Ed25519 attestation.
Report tampering or Git SHA substitution is detected by verification.
failuresLessons: A green transport test suite is necessary but not enough to summarize crash semantics for later Qubes qualification; a fixed evidence contract prevents omissions.
The report must not convert claim/heartbeat/fail indeterminate outcomes into success. Those operations remain not-exactly-once after unknown post-mutation death.
A local SHA-256 report digest proves integrity/comparability, not trusted origin. Protocol-origin authentication remains the Ed25519 response attestation.
Adding a new report-signing key now would add operational/key-management risk without closing the underlying transaction gap.
safety: Synthetic/defensive transport qualification only. No real financial transactions, payment data, fraud workflows, or weakened security controls.
